Chapter V

Life On and Off the Campus

Although the major objective in a study of the history of a college may properly be that of defining its character and evaluating its contribution to the advancement of education, an important supporting aim ranking as a close second may legitimately be that of finding beneath the abstract surface of its educational aspects the lively ebb and flow of human activity in its halls and on the campus. The effective years of Savoy Male and Female College are just far enough back to permit a historical perspective in the treatment of its place in the history of education in Texas and far enough back to facilitate that research. On the other hand, its life and history are, happily, much too recent to be a matter solely of written record; for first-hand pictures of life in its environs have been available. Its story in Chapter III is told of the activities of Savoy College realistically at work and at play—and to do so wherever possible on the basis of personal recollections in response of ex-students to the author's request for reminiscences.⁶⁴

Although this material is rather of sociological than scientific interest, a different treatment might deprive it of much personal significance. Such a treatment might find its own purpose, for, in the following story will show a certain continuing and ever present side of the life at the college beyond the ordinary activities—the temperance, literary, and debating societies —then they take up the out of school activities of individual students, and finally the activities of alumni.

⁶⁴"Rare items may have come from the students' memoirs, but the actual research for this chapter was done from students' letters, printed in The Plainsman Messenger of April 28 and May 5, 1888, and published in The Plainsman Messenger Supplement, in March, 1938, edited and published by the Bureau of Education," in The Executive Documents of the Senate of the United States. The reference elsewhere is to the College library since it was the one in which the book is held, including as it was the actual citation.
